Theorem 4.3 should be compared with [Hwa96, Theorem 1], which studies another regime of deviations in the mod-φ setting, namely, when h goes to zero (or equivalently, x →η′(0)). We shall also look at this regime in our Theorem 4.8.

The main difference between Theorems 3.4 and 4.3 is the replacement of the factor ψ(h)/(1 −e−h) by ψ(h)/h; the same happens with Bahadur-Rao’s estimates when going from lattice distributions to non-lattice distributions.

Let (Xn)n∈N be a sequence of random variables that converges mod-φ with pa- rameters (tn)n∈N and limiting function ψ, on a strip S(c,d) that does not necessarily contain 0. For h ∈(c, d), we make the exponential change of measure Q[dy] = ehy ϕXn(h) P[Xn ∈dy], and denote eXn a random variable following this law. The sequence ( eXn)n∈N converges mod-eφ, where eφ is the inﬁnitely divisible distribution with characteristic function eη(z+h)−η(h). The parameters of this new mod-convergence are again (tn)n∈N, and the limiting function is eψ(z) = ψ(z + h) ψ(h) . The new mod-eφ convergence occurs in the strip S(c−h,d−h).
candidates.proof_excerpt: Obvious since ϕ eXn(z) = ϕXn(z + h)/ϕXn(h).

candidates.statement: Consider a non-constant inﬁnitely divisible law φ, of type non-lattice, with a convergent moment generating function in a strip S(c,d) with c < 0 < d. We also assume that φ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. Then, there exists a constant D > 0 only depending on φ, and an interval (−ε, ε) ⊂(c, d), such that for all h ∈(−ε, ε), and all δ small enough, qδ = max u∈R\(−δ,δ) | exp(η(h + iu) −η(h))| ≤1 −D δ2.
